I’ll reconstruct the endpoint permutation directly from the oriented smooth strands, then compute the hypermap cycles and block matrix exactly. I’ll also verify the spectral polynomial’s irreducibility independently, since the characteristic polynomial alone is insufficient here.
answer: \(\mathcal S=(5,\;t^4-9t-36)\)

reasoning: The oriented strands give
\[
\sigma=(x_1\,x_4\,x_{11}\,x_8\,x_2\,x_5\,x_{10}\,x_7\,x_3\,x_6\,x_9),
\]
so \(c(\sigma)=1\), while \(c(r)=1\). Applying \(\sigma\) first and then \(r\),
\[
r\sigma=(x_1\,x_5\,x_{11}\,x_9\,x_2\,x_6\,x_{10}\,x_8\,x_3\,x_7\,x_4),
\]
hence \(c((r\sigma)^{-1})=1\). Therefore
\[
2-2g=1+1+1-11=-8,
\]
so \(g=5\). The block matrix is
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}
0&3&0&0\\
0&0&1&2\\
3&0&0&0\\
0&0&2&0
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\det(tI-M)=t^4-9t-36.
\]
Its reduction modulo \(5\) is \(t^4+t+4\). It has no roots in \(\mathbb F_5\); a possible quadratic factorization would be
\[
(t^2+at+b)(t^2-at+d),
\]
with \(bd=4\), \(a(d-b)=1\), and \(b+d=a^2\). The possibilities \((b,d)=(2,2),(3,3)\) violate the second condition, while \((1,4),(4,1)\) force \(a^2=4\) but \(b+d=0\), violating the third. Thus the reduction is irreducible over \(\mathbb F_5\), so \(t^4-9t-36\) is irreducible over \(\mathbb Q\). Since \(M\) is nonnegative and irreducible, its spectral radius is an eigenvalue, giving \(m_\rho(t)=t^4-9t-36\).

answer: \(\mathcal S=(3,\ t^4-9t-36)\)

reasoning: The oriented strands give
\[
\sigma=(x_1\,x_4\,x_{10}\,x_7)(x_2\,x_5\,x_{11}\,x_8)(x_3\,x_6\,x_9),
\]
so \(c(\sigma)=3\), while \(c(r)=1\). Applying \(\sigma\) first and then \(r\),
\[
r\sigma=(x_1\,x_5)(x_2\,x_6\,x_{10}\,x_8\,x_3\,x_7)(x_4\,x_{11}\,x_9),
\]
hence \(c((r\sigma)^{-1})=3\). Therefore
\[
2-2g=1+3+3-11=-4,
\]
so \(g=3\).

The block matrix is
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}
0&3&0&0\\
0&0&1&2\\
3&0&0&0\\
0&0&2&0
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its characteristic polynomial is
\[
f(t)=\det(tI-M)=t^4-9t-36.
\]
The matrix is nonnegative and irreducible, so its spectral radius \(\rho\) is an eigenvalue and satisfies \(f(\rho)=0\). Modulo \(7\),
\[
\bar f(t)=t^4+5t+6.
\]
Its values at \(0,1,\ldots,6\) are \(6,5,4,4,2,5,2\), so it has no linear factor. If it factored into monic quadratics, it would have the form \((t^2+at+b)(t^2-at+d)\), with \(bd=6\), \(a(d-b)=5\), and \(b+d-a^2=0\). For the six ordered pairs \((b,d)\) with \(bd=6\), the resulting values of \(b+d-a^2\) are \(6,1,1,5,5,6\), never \(0\). Thus \(\bar f\), and therefore \(f\), is irreducible over \(\mathbb Q\). Hence \(m_\rho(t)=t^4-9t-36\).
